cards.text: Friend, Jeremiah the prophet has been carrying the LORD's word to nation after nation. Now the LORD speaks through him about the big one: Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans. And I'll tell you right now, this word does NOT read like a fan letter.

cards.question: The LORD says to announce it to the nations, lift up a banner and hold nothing back. What's the big news about Babylon?

cards.text: Captured. And the news doesn't stop at the city. Babylon's own gods get named in the announcement too: Bel and Marduk.

cards.question: In the announcement about Babylon's fall, Babylon's idols come through the whole thing in one piece.

cards.text: Bel is put to shame, and Marduk is shattered. Friend, when the news puts SHATTERED right next to your god's name, it might be time to rethink some things. Then the LORD says who's coming against Babylon: a nation.

cards.question: A nation from the ___ will come against Babylon and make her land a desolation.

cards.text: No one will live in that land, and man and beast both flee. Then, "In those days and at that time," the LORD turns to His own people.

cards.question: In those days, who comes together, weeping as they come, to seek the LORD their God?

answers.text: The children of Israel and Judah
The people of Moab and Edom

cards.question: Israel and Judah ask for directions as they seek the LORD. Which way do they turn their faces?
When Israel and Judah join themselves to the LORD, it's in a covenant that will run out someday.

cards.text: Then the LORD says how they got so lost: "My people are lost sheep; their shepherds have led them astray," wandering from mountain to hill. That's following a GPS that keeps saying "recalculating" until you're three towns past where you started.

cards.question: After all that wandering, the LORD's lost sheep have forgotten their ___ place.

cards.text: Anyone who finds these sheep devours them. And their enemies already have a speech ready.

cards.question: What do Israel's enemies say about devouring them?

answers.text: We're not guilty since they sinned against the LORD
We were only following our own king's orders
They came and attacked our land first

cards.text: Not guilty. That's denting somebody's car in the parking lot and leaving a note that says, "You shouldn't have parked there." And even those enemies call the LORD Israel's "true pasture."

cards.question: The LORD tells His people to flee from the midst of Babylon. As they go, what should they be like?

answers.text: Lambs that trail behind the flock
Sheep that stay inside the pen

cards.question: Why is it time for the LORD's people to get out of Babylon?

answers.text: God is bringing great nations against her
A famine is about to sweep her land
Babylon is about to close her gates

cards.text: Those nations line up against her, and their arrows are like skilled warriors who don't come back empty-handed. Every shot delivers, which is more than I could say for my stamps my last year on the Millers' counter.

cards.question: When Chaldea is plundered, the ones who plunder her walk away with barely anything.

cards.text: Now the LORD talks straight to the ones who plunder His inheritance, rejoicing and singing in triumph, frolicking like a heifer treading grain and neighing like stallions. That's a whole empire doing a victory dance in the end zone. LOUD.

cards.question: Because of all that celebrating, Babylon, the mother of those plunderers, will be the ___ of the nations.
Because of the LORD's wrath, Babylon ends up a desert nobody lives in. People passing through will stop to admire what's left of her.

cards.text: Then the LORD calls out every archer: line up around Babylon, shoot at her, spare no arrows.

cards.question: Why does the LORD tell the archers to spare no arrows at Babylon?

answers.text: She has sinned against the LORD
She has run low on soldiers

cards.text: Next comes the order to raise a war cry against her on every side.

cards.question: As the war cry goes up all around her, what does Babylon do?

answers.text: She throws up her hands in surrender
She calls on her allies for help
She fires back from her high towers

cards.text: Her towers have fallen and her walls are torn down. I haven't seen things come down that fast since I stacked twelve cookie boxes on a wobbly counter and called it a display.

cards.question: This is the vengeance of the LORD: as Babylon has done, do the ___ to her.

cards.text: Even the farm work stops. The sower and the one who wields the sickle at harvest time get cut off from Babylon.

cards.question: In the face of the oppressor's sword, each person in Babylon flees to his own people and his own land.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Israel's story in one picture: "Israel is a scattered flock, chased away by lions."

cards.question: Who was the first to devour Israel?

cards.text: And the last to crush Israel's bones? Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. So now the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, has something to say about that king.

cards.question: The LORD says He will punish the king of Babylon and his land just as He punished the king of Assyria.

cards.text: Then the scattered flock comes home. The LORD will return Israel to his pasture, to graze on Carmel and Bashan.

cards.question: Back home on the hills of Ephraim and Gilead, how does Israel's soul end up?

cards.text: From lost sheep to a satisfied soul on the hills. I know that one, friend: one night I'm sharing a drawer with dead batteries, and in a blink I've got a whole planet and a sky to myself.

cards.question: In those days, says the LORD, a search will be made for Israel's ___, but there will be ___.

cards.text: Why? The LORD says, "for I will forgive the remnant I preserve." And trust me, friend, this word against Babylon is just getting started.

findings.problem: The card says Jeremiah 'has been carrying the LORD's word to nation after nation.' That is a fact from outside the passage (the oracles in Jeremiah 46-49), and the card gives no reference for it. The card cites only Jeremiah 50:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences. It is not the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup line 'the LORD turns to His own people' rules out both wrong answers on card 8 (the Chaldeans and their kings, the people of Moab and Edom). That gives the answer away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Not guilty.', the parking-lot joke, and the 'true pasture' line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke depends on knowing that his stamps went blurry during his last year on the Millers' counter. Nothing earlier in this lesson sets that up. Onboarding only guarantees that bakers know about his years in the junk drawer.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences, counting 'LOUD.' Only the opening card of Prep can have three, and this card opens stop 2, not Prep.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'I haven't seen things come down that fast' says Babylon's towers and walls fell quickly. Jeremiah 50:15 says nothing about how fast they fell.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The question says 'each person in Babylon' flees to his own people. Jeremiah 50:16 says only 'each will turn to his own people, each will flee to his own land.' The text doesn't say who 'each' is. The question also changes 'turn to his own people' into fleeing to his own people.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the question, 'Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.', and the 'So now the LORD of Hosts' line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: No earlier card in stop 2 sets up sin, guilt or a search, so the baker has nothing to reason from. Several other combinations read just as naturally, such as 'Israel's heroes, but there will be none' or 'Israel's gold, but there will be plenty.' The pick comes down to luck.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Why?', the forgiveness quote, and the line that says the story isn't over.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
